subject: Request: Clarify standby obligations & recovery scope for multi-region DR
messages:
From: Lena Marks <lena.marks@finbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Steve Cho <s.cho@finbank.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Clarify standby obligations & recovery scope for multi-region DR

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our security and ops teams reviewed Redwood’s standard multi-region SLA and identified a few areas that need contract language to reflect FinBank’s regulatory posture in the EU. Specifically:

- We need clarity on the conditions that trigger automatic failover vs. manual activation of the warm standby in the US region.
- Desired RTO for mission-critical routing: 2 hours from failover decision.
- Desired RPO: no more than 1 hour for transaction metadata and 4 hours for batch analytics.
- Requirement for a quarterly failover test that includes a read-only switchover and data recovery verification.

We understand some of these are outside Redwood’s standard hosted SLA and expect an exception/addendum. Can you outline what Redwood would accept as an amendment, the test plan cadence, and any operational responsibilities FinBank will need to take on?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to finalize terms by mid-December.

Best,
Lena Marks
Head of Platform Security
FinBank

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Marks <lena.marks@finbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarify standby obligations & recovery scope for multi-region DR

Lena —

Thanks for laying out the requirements. We can support a tailored amendment for FinBank. High-level response below, and I’ve copied Marissa (account lead) to coordinate the formal redline and Aditya (product ops) for the test plan details.

Summary of what Redwood can offer (subject to contract language and capacity reservation):
- Failover model: We propose a policy-based activation: automatic failover for infrastructure-level region outages (loss of >= 2 availability zones or region-wide scheduler failures) and customer-initiated/manual activation for application-layer incidents. We will include a clause defining the detection windows and an SLA decision workflow.
- RTO/RPO: We can commit to a 2-hour RTO for the warm standby for the FinBank production route, conditioned on (a) FinBank maintaining the recommended KV-cache warm window, and (b) using the dedicated reserved capacity pool in the target region. RPO target of <=1 hour for transaction metadata is achievable with continuous cross-region replication; analytics RPO of 4 hours is doable if batch replication is configured.
- Quarterly testing: Redwood will support a quarterly read-only switchover and a one-time full failover drill per year. Tests will be scheduled in collaboration; we propose a 60-day test window prior to signing to validate operational steps.
- Responsibilities: FinBank needs to allow test traffic, maintain a guarded rollback plan, and provide a runbook contact list for exercise coordination. Redwood will provide runbook templates and a shared timeline for canary and bulk traffic cutover.

Open items we need to resolve before we draft the amendment:
1) Whether FinBank requires SLA financial credits for missed RTO/RPO (we typically offer service credits tied to availability windows; carve-outs possible for targeted routes).
2) Exact definitions of "failover decision" and measurement start time (e.g., detection vs. declared incident).
3) Confirmation that FinBank will purchase the reserved capacity pool in the secondary region during the commitment window.

I’ve attached a preliminary amendment draft and a proposed test plan spreadsheet for operational sign-off. Marissa — can you pick this up and propose next steps?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RBW_FinBank_DR_Amendment_draft_v1.pdf
Attachment: standby-test-plan.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Marks <lena.marks@finbank.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarify standby obligations & recovery scope for multi-region DR

Hi Lena —

Following up with the next concrete steps so procurement can track timelines. Appreciate your clarity on the RTO/RPO targets. Proposed plan:

1) Commercial ask: FinBank confirms commitment to the reserved capacity SKU in the US-west region for the warm standby. We will then scope the amendment to include the 2hr RTO / 1hr RPO targets for the specified production route.
2) Legal/procurement: We’ll propose Service Credit language limited to the affected route (capped) to address missed RTOs. If FinBank requires unlimited liability we’ll need to escalate to leadership (Kimberly copied).
3) Operational test: Schedule a 60–90 minute read-only failover test during the proposed quarter window. Aditya — please find an initial test script in the attached spreadsheet.

Can we target an initial joint test week: Dec 14–18? If that works, please confirm the times FinBank prefers (we recommend EU off-peak window: 01:00–05:00 UTC).

If procurement wants to see a redline, we can deliver a first-pass contract amendment by Dec 6.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Marks <lena.marks@finbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Steve Cho <s.cho@finbank.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 17:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarify standby obligations & recovery scope for multi-region DR

Marissa, Jonas —

Thanks. Dec 14–18 works for the joint read-only test window; FinBank prefers 02:00–04:00 UTC on Dec 15 if that slot is available. We’ll confirm reserved capacity purchase internally by EOD Dec 7 — procurement asked for the formal amendment redline ahead of approval, so the Dec 6 deliverable is helpful.

On credits: FinBank’s policy is to request route-specific service credits for SLA misses up to a defined cap. We’re not asking for unlimited liability. Please include a sample credit schedule in the amendment (e.g., % credit tiers for missed RTO buckets).

Two small asks for the test plan:
- Include a verification step to confirm KV-cache warming state prior to failover.
- Add a rollback timebox and explicit ownership for DNS/traffic reroute during the exercise.

If you can incorporate those items in the redline, we’ll expedite internal approvals.

Best,
Lena Marks
Head of Platform Security
FinBank
